summary: PayPal SANDBOX integration validated. 12/12 pytest cases pass. PUT /api/wallet/paypal-email accepts valid email (200 + persisted in GET /api/wallet) and rejects 'notanemail' with 400 invalid_email; unauthenticated returns 401. POST /api/bookings/{id}/paypal/create: unknown id -> 404 booking_not_found; UNPAID booking owned by demo-preview-token-123 -> 200 with real order_id (PayPal shape) + approval url on www.sandbox.paypal.com; same booking with biz-test-token-999 -> 403 forbidden. POST /api/bookings/{id}/payout: called by non-provider (client) -> 403 forbidden; called by unrelated user (biz) -> 403 forbidden; called by actual provider on UNPAID booking -> 400 not_paid (verified after seeding a provider session with paypal_email); unknown id -> 404. Sanity: GET /api/categories and GET /api/bookings still 200. Buyer approval + capture and full payout success intentionally NOT tested (no sandbox buyer available, per request).
action_items: Consider capturing an order via a manual sandbox buyer approval when possible, to exercise POST /api/paypal/capture/{order_id} (currently only creation + permission branches were validated).
Optional: add server-side email regex/validator for paypal-email (currently only '@' check) — e.g. reject 'a@' or '@b'.
critical_code_review_comments: payments_paypal.set_paypal_email: validation is '@' in email only — accepts '@' alone, 'a@' or '@b'. Consider stricter validation (pydantic EmailStr or regex).
payments_paypal.create_paypal_order: currency is hard-coded 'EUR' — matches JOBBY's Italy scope; fine for MVP but note if multi-currency comes later.

payments_paypal.capture_paypal_order: no auth check that the caller is the booking customer (any authenticated user with a valid order_id could trigger a capture attempt). Consider verifying tx['user_id'] == user['user_id'] before calling PayPal capture.
payments_paypal.payout_provider: correct guards (not owner -> 403, not paid -> 400, already paid out -> 400, no paypal_email -> 400). Good.
PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID/PAYPAL_SECRET read at import time via os.environ.get(..., '') — silently empties if unset. Consider raising at startup if PayPal router is registered but creds missing.
seed_data_creation: Temporary user_sessions doc created for provider prov_85f40cbec39e (session_token 'TEST_prov_token_bec39e', expires_at=+1d) to test payout not_paid branch. Doc is deleted in test teardown. Also set paypal_email on that provider's users doc for test purposes (persists — safe/no side effects on business logic).
context_for_next_testing_agent: PayPal sandbox creds are live in /app/backend/.env (PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/BASE). Real orders are created against api-m.sandbox.paypal.com and approve URLs are on www.sandbox.paypal.com. To fully exercise capture and payout, a PayPal sandbox buyer login is required. The demo-preview account now has paypal_email='x@paypal.com'. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_paypal_integration.py — reusable for regressions.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. All 4 requested paths (paypal-email set + validate, create order 200/403/404, payout 403/400/404, sanity) behave exactly as specified.
